# Facilitator Guide — AI Productivity Workflows

Slides: `slides/slides.md`. Demos: `demos/`. Exercise sheets: `exercises.md`. Every demo runs offline; start times assume 09:30.

**One week before:** run `python demos/run_all.py`. Confirm room, projector, one laptop per pair, Wi-Fi. Print exercises and handouts.

## Day 1

| Time | Segment | What you do and say |
|---|---|---|
| 09:30 | Welcome | Outcomes on the first slide. Ask each table for the one question they want answered; write them on the flipchart. |
| 09:40 | **Module 1 — Meetings and email** | Teach: transcription, summaries, action extraction, replies in your voice. |
| 10:01 | Demo 1 | **Run `python demos/01_meeting_to_followups.py`** — owner/action/date extraction from a transcript, the gaps it refuses to guess, and one follow-up per owner. Close with: *“The model is a good note-taker and a bad mind-reader. If nobody said a date, the right output is a question.”* |
| 10:16 | Lab 1 | Meeting → actions → follow-ups — see `exercises.md`. Walk the room; collect one result per table. |
| 10:40 | **Module 2 — Documents and spreadsheets** | Teach: drafting, structured extraction, formula help, analysis with verification. |
| 11:19 | Break |  |

Close with: *“Let AI write the sentence. Make it show you where each number came from. 'Under 4 months' was never in my notes.”* |
| 11:49 | Lab 2 | Report from raw notes — see `exercises.md`. Walk the room; collect one result per table. |

Close with: *“AI can fill the table in a minute. Your job is the weights, the sources and the one question: what would change our mind?”* |
| 13:46 | Lab 3 | Vendor comparison brief — see `exercises.md`. Walk the room; collect one result per table. |
| 14:10 | **Module 4 — Your personal system** | Teach: prompt library, templates, review habits. |

| 14:28 | Lab 4 | Save 5 workflows — see `exercises.md`. Walk the room; collect one result per table. |
| 14:40 | Close | Assessment: Submitted workflow library. Return to the flipchart questions — tick the ones answered. |

## If short on time

Keep every demo; shorten the teaching before it. Cut labs to a paired discussion of the lab question rather than dropping them. Never cut the close.

## What can go wrong

- **A demo fails on the day** — you ran `run_all.py` last week, so it is the environment: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, then re-run. Screenshots of each output live in nobody's folder: take them after your dry run.
- **No projector / terminal too small** — open `/demos` in a browser and run the same demo from the *Course labs* section.
- **The room has no laptops** — run labs as table discussions using the printed exercise sheet; you run the script and change the inputs they call out.
